VI.}}|{{sc|according to s. iohn.}}|235}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=6|verse=50}} This is the bread that de{{ls}}cendeth from heauen: that if any man eate of it, he die not. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=51}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Go{{ls}}pel in a daily Ma{{ls}}{{ls}}e for the dead.}}∷ I am the liuing bread, that came dovvne from heauen. If any man eate of this bread, he {{ls}}hal liue for euer: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 26. Mr. 14, 22. Lu. 22, 19. 1. Cor. 11, 24.''}}* the bread vvhich I vvil giue, is my fle{{ls}}h for the life of the vvorld.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=52}} The Ievves therfore {{ls}}troue among them {{ls}}elues, {{ls}}aying, {{sup|‖}} Hovv can this man giue vs his fle{{ls}}h to eate? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=53}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aid to them, Amen, amen I {{ls}}ay to you, {{sup|‖}} Vnles you eate the fle{{ls}}h of the Sonne of man, {{sup|‖}} and drinke his bloud, {{sup|‖}} you {{ls}}hal not haue life in you. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=54}} He that eateth my fle{{ls}}h, and drinketh my bloud, hath life euerla{{ls}}ting: and {{sup|‖}} I vvil rai{{ls}}e him vp in the la{{ls}}t day.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=55}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō {{sc|Corpvs christi}} day.}}For my fle{{ls}}h, is {{sup|‖}} meate in deede: and my bloud is drinke in deede. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=56}} He that eateth my fle{{ls}}h, and drinketh my bloud, abideth in me, and I in him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=57}} As the liuing father hath {{ls}}ent me, and I liue by the father: and he that eateth me, the {{ls}}ame al{{ls}}o {{ls}}hal liue by me. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=58}} This is the bread that came dovvne from heauen. Not as your fathers did eate Manna, and died. {{sup|‖}} He that eateth this bread, {{ls}}hal liue for euer.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=59}} The{{ls}}e things he {{ls}}aid teaching in the Synagogue, in Capharnáum.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=60}} Many therfore of his Di{{ls}}ciples hearing it, {{ls}}aid, This {{ls}}aying is hard, and vvho can heare it? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=61}} But {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving vvith him {{ls}}elf that his Di{{ls}}ciples murmured at this, he {{ls}}aid to them, Doth this {{ls}}candalize you? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=62}} {{sup|‖}} If then you {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ee {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 3, 13.''}}* the Sonne of man a{{ls}}cend vvhere he vvas before? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=63}} It is the {{ls}}pirit that quickeneth, {{sup|‖}} the fle{{ls}}h profiteth nothing. The wordes that I haue {{ls}}poken to you, be {{ls}}pirit and life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=64}} But there be certaine of you {{sup|‖}} that beleeue not. For {{sc|Iesvs}} knevv from the beginning vvho they vvere that did not beleeue, and vvho he vvas that vvould betray him. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=65}} And he {{ls}}aid, Therfore did I {{ls}}ay to you, that no man can come to me, vnles it be giuen him of my Father. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=66}} After this many of his Di{{ls}}ciples {{sup|‖}} vvent backe: and novv they vvalked not vvith him.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=67}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aid to the Tvvelue, VVhat, vvil you al{{ls}}o depart? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=68}} Simon {{sup|‖}} Peter therfore an{{ls}}vvered him, Lord, to vvhom {{ls}}hal vve goe? thou ha{{ls}}t the vvordes of eternal life. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=69}} And we beleeue and haue knovven that thou art Chri{{ls}}t the {{ls}}onne of God. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=70}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered them, Haue not I cho{{ls}}en you the Tvvelue: & of you one is a deuil? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=71}} And he meant Iudas I{{ls}}cariot, Simons {{ls}}onne: for this {{ls}}ame vvas to betray him, vvhereas he vvas one of the Tvvelue.
